newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm on dollar on exporter sales.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm on dollar on exporter sales.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling firmed against the dollar on Thursday boosted by inflows from coffee and tea export auctions, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.91 against the dollar from 54.92 on Wednesday, while on the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 87.81 compared to 87.47.
"Sentiment looks positive for a stronger shilling," a dealer said. "Especially if demand remains at current levels, very low, unable to move the market."
"There is very little dollar-buying interest as importers have shied off the market," another dealer said.
Some dealers said the shilling was rangebound at the 54.85/55.00 level.
The money market was still tight with overnight rates quoted above 15 percent unchanged.
